title: Detecting semilinear dual maps on a scalar-extension basis
statement: Let T be a scheme and take its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let alpha : R → S be a map of commutative ring sheaves, M and P R-module sheaves, and Q an S-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose e : S tensor_R P ≅ Q for the actual scalar extension [def-sp-scalar-tensor-comparison-data]. Let c and d be R-linear maps from M to the restriction along alpha of the internal S-dual of Q [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. If, for every site object U, phi in M(U), and x in P(U), the values of c(phi) and d(phi) agree on e(1 tensor x), evaluated on the identity object of the slice over U, then c = d. Neither local freeness nor an invertibility assumption on M or P is needed.

source.place: lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict and section-tensor-product (03EK, 03EL); explicit transport/extensionality consequence used in the coefficient-twist scalar construction.

proof.text: Extend c and d by the scalar-extension lifting property to S-linear maps F and G from the extension of M to the internal dual of Q. Precompose dual functionals with e, giving an isomorphism from that dual to the dual of the extension of P.

Apply scalarExtensionDual_hom_ext to F and G after that internal-Hom isomorphism. Its scalar pure tensors in both arguments reduce by linearity and scalarExtensionLift_tmul to evaluations of c and d on e(1 tensor x), multiplied by the two target scalar coefficients. The hypothesis gives equality. Cancel the internal-Hom isomorphism, then evaluate F=G on 1 tensor phi and use scalarExtensionLift_tmul to obtain c=d.

proof_origin.place: Scalar comparison and its tensor normalization. A proved helper extracted after profiling and local instance caches did not bring the enlarged item below the 60-second limit.

mathlib_searches.query: Two semilinear sheaf module maps to an internal dual agree if their evaluations agree on a scalar extension basis
mathlib_searches.results: Eight sheaf-module extensionality hits, headed by SheafOfModules.hom_ext and hom_ext_iff. None detects sections of an internal dual on scalar-extension generators.
One hit, ModuleCat.hom_ext in Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Basic: equality of the underlying linear maps detects module-category morphisms. It does not supply scalar-dual generation.

One unrelated exterior-power comment in Mathlib. Local search found a proved private semilinear_dual_ext in ScalarExtensionFunctor; importing that module would cycle, so its short generic proof is preserved in this independent module.

mathlib_searches.query: Maps into an internal dual are equal when their evaluations agree on scalar extension tensor generators
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits including Module.Dual.eval_apply, IsBaseChange.toDualBaseChange_tmul and dualTensorHomEquivOfBasis. These concern ordinary module duals and do not state the internal sheaf-dual extensionality used here.

from.place: Scalar extension of the first root line and its tensor and dual constructions; this helper transports the scalar comparison or proves its dual uniqueness.

lean.statement:
theorem scalarSemilinearDualExt
    (T : Scheme.{u}) {R S : Sheaf (ProEt.topology T) CommRingCat.{u + 1}}
    (α : R ⟶ S) (M P : proEtaleRingModules T R) (Q : proEtaleRingModules T S)
    (e : SheafOfModules.changeOfRingsOfUniverses.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u + 1} α P ≅ Q)
    (c d : M ⟶ (SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u + 1}
      ((sheafCompose (ProEt.topology T) (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).map α)).obj
      ((SheafOfModules.homFunctor (R := S)).obj (Opposite.op Q) |>.obj
        (SheafOfModules.unit _)))
    (h : ∀ (U : T.ProEtᵒᵖ) (φ : M.val.obj U) (x : P.val.obj U),
      ((c.val.app U φ).app (Opposite.op (Over.mk (𝟙 U.unop))))
          (e.hom.val.app U
            (SheafOfModules.scalarExtensionSection.{u + 1, u, u + 1, u + 1} α P U 1 x)) =
        ((d.val.app U φ).app (Opposite.op (Over.mk (𝟙 U.unop))))
          (e.hom.val.app U
            (SheafOfModules.scalarExtensionSection.{u + 1, u, u + 1, u + 1} α P U 1 x))) :
    c = d
